Let \(x\) be the number of bacteria present at time \(t\) (hours).

The rate of increase is proportional to the number present:
\(\dfrac{dx}{dt} = kx\), where \(k > 0\) is the constant of proportionality.

Separating variables and integrating:
\(\dfrac{dx}{x} = k\,dt \implies \log x = kt + c\).

Let the initial number be \(x_0\) (at \(t = 0\)), so \(c = \log x_0\) and
\(\log\left(\dfrac{x}{x_0}\right) = kt\), i.e. \(x = x_0\, e^{kt}\).

Given: the number doubles in 4 hours, so at \(t = 4\), \(x = 2x_0\):
\(2x_0 = x_0\, e^{4k} \implies e^{4k} = 2\).

Number after 12 hours:
\(x = x_0\, e^{12k} = x_0\left(e^{4k}\right)^{3} = x_0\,(2)^{3} = 8x_0\).

Hence the bacteria increase to 8 times the original number in 12 hours.

Let \(r\) be the radius of the spherical raindrop at time \(t\) (hours).

Volume \(V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}\) and surface area \(S = 4\pi r^{2}\).

The drop evaporates at a rate proportional to its surface area:
\(\dfrac{dV}{dt} = -k\,S\), where \(k > 0\) (mass decreasing).

Now \(\dfrac{dV}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}\right) = 4\pi r^{2}\,\dfrac{dr}{dt}\).

Therefore \(4\pi r^{2}\,\dfrac{dr}{dt} = -k\,(4\pi r^{2})\), which gives
\(\dfrac{dr}{dt} = -k\).

Integrating: \(r = -kt + c\).

At \(t = 0\), \(r = 3\) mm, so \(c = 3\), giving \(r = 3 - kt\).

At \(t = 1\), \(r = 2\) mm: \(2 = 3 - k \implies k = 1\).

Hence the radius at any time \(t\) is
\(r = 3 - t\) (mm), valid for \(0 \le t \le 3\).

Let \(P\) be the population of the city at time \(t\) (years).

The rate of growth is proportional to the population:
\(\dfrac{dP}{dt} = kP\), with constant of proportionality \(k = 0.04\).

Separating variables and integrating:
\(\dfrac{dP}{P} = k\,dt \implies \log P = kt + c\).

With initial population \(P_0\) at \(t = 0\), \(c = \log P_0\), so
\(P = P_0\, e^{kt}\).

Here \(P_0 = 10{,}000\) and \(k = 0.04\), so after \(t = 25\) years:
\(P = 10{,}000\, e^{0.04 \times 25} = 10{,}000\, e^{1}\).

Taking \(e = 2.7182\):
\(P = 10{,}000 \times 2.7182 = 27{,}182\).

Hence the population of the city after 25 years is 27,182.

Let \(m\) be the amount of radium present at time \(t\) (years).

Radium decomposes at a rate proportional to the amount present:
\(\dfrac{dm}{dt} = -k\,m\), where \(k > 0\).

Separating variables and integrating:
\(\dfrac{dm}{m} = -k\,dt \implies \log m = -kt + c\).

Let the initial amount be \(m_0\) at \(t = 0\); then \(c = \log m_0\) and
\(m = m_0\, e^{-kt}\).

Given: \(p\) percent disappears in one year, so at \(t = 1\), the amount left is
\(m_0\left(1 - \dfrac{p}{100}\right)\):
\(m_0\, e^{-k} = m_0\left(1 - \dfrac{p}{100}\right) \implies e^{-k} = 1 - \dfrac{p}{100}\).

Amount left after 2 years:
\(m = m_0\, e^{-2k} = m_0\left(e^{-k}\right)^{2} = m_0\left(1 - \dfrac{p}{100}\right)^{2}\).

As a percentage of the original amount, the radium left after 2 years is
\(\left(1 - \dfrac{p}{100}\right)^{2} \times 100 = \dfrac{(100 - p)^{2}}{100}\) percent.

Let \(P\) be the number of inhabitants at time \(t\) (years).

The rate of increase is proportional to the number of inhabitants:
\(\dfrac{dP}{dt} = kP\), where \(k > 0\).

Integrating: \(\log P = kt + c\). With initial population \(P_0\) at \(t = 0\),
\(P = P_0\, e^{kt}\).

The population doubles in 60 years, so at \(t = 60\), \(P = 2P_0\):
\(2P_0 = P_0\, e^{60k} \implies e^{60k} = 2 \implies 60k = \log 2 \implies k = \dfrac{\log 2}{60}\).

Let the population treble (become \(3P_0\)) after \(t\) years:
\(3P_0 = P_0\, e^{kt} \implies e^{kt} = 3 \implies kt = \log 3\).

Therefore
\(t = \dfrac{\log 3}{k} = \dfrac{\log 3}{\log 2 / 60} = 60 \times \dfrac{\log 3}{\log 2}\).

Using \(\log 2 = 0.6912\) and \(\log 3 = 1.0986\):
\(t = 60 \times \dfrac{1.0986}{0.6912} = 60 \times 1.5894 = 95.36\) years (approximately).

Hence the population will treble in about 95.36 years.

Let \(\theta\) be the temperature of the body (in degrees Celsius) at time \(t\) (minutes). Room (surrounding) temperature \(\theta_0 = 25^\circ\).

By Newton's law of cooling:
\(\dfrac{d\theta}{dt} = -k(\theta - \theta_0) = -k(\theta - 25)\), where \(k > 0\).

Separating variables and integrating:
\(\dfrac{d\theta}{\theta - 25} = -k\,dt \implies \log(\theta - 25) = -kt + c\),
giving \(\theta - 25 = C\, e^{-kt}\).

At \(t = 0\), \(\theta = 80^\circ\): \(80 - 25 = C \implies C = 55\).
So \(\theta - 25 = 55\, e^{-kt}\).

At \(t = 30\) minutes, \(\theta = 50^\circ\):
\(50 - 25 = 55\, e^{-30k} \implies 25 = 55\, e^{-30k} \implies e^{-30k} = \dfrac{25}{55} = \dfrac{5}{11}\).

After 1 hour, i.e. \(t = 60\) minutes:
\(\theta - 25 = 55\, e^{-60k} = 55\left(e^{-30k}\right)^{2} = 55\left(\dfrac{5}{11}\right)^{2} = 55 \times \dfrac{25}{121} = \dfrac{125}{11}\).

Thus \(\theta = 25 + \dfrac{125}{11} = 25 + 11.36 = 36.36^\circ\) C (approximately).

Hence the temperature of the body after 1 hour is about \(36.36^\circ\) C.

Let \(N\) be the number of bacteria present at time \(t\) (hours).

The rate of growth is proportional to the number present:
\(\dfrac{dN}{dt} = kN\), where \(k > 0\).

Integrating: \(\log N = kt + c\), so \(N = N_0\, e^{kt}\), where \(N_0\) is the initial number.

Here \(N_0 = 1000\). The number doubles in 1 hour, so at \(t = 1\), \(N = 2000\):
\(2000 = 1000\, e^{k} \implies e^{k} = 2\).

Thus \(N = 1000\,(e^{k})^{t} = 1000\,(2)^{t}\).

After \(t = 2\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{5}{2}\) hours:
\(N = 1000 \times 2^{5/2} = 1000 \times 2^{2} \times 2^{1/2} = 1000 \times 4 \times \sqrt{2}\).

Taking \(\sqrt{2} = 1.414\):
\(N = 1000 \times 4 \times 1.414 = 5656\).

Hence the number of bacteria after \(2\dfrac{1}{2}\) hours is 5656.

Let \(m\) be the mass (in gm) of the radioactive element at time \(t\).

The rate of disintegration is proportional to the mass present:
\(\dfrac{dm}{dt} = -k\,m\), where \(k > 0\) is the decay constant.

Separating variables and integrating:
\(\dfrac{dm}{m} = -k\,dt \implies \log m = -kt + c\).

At \(t = 0\), the original mass \(m = 1.5\) gm, so \(c = \log 1.5\) and
\(\log m - \log 1.5 = -kt\), i.e. \(\log\left(\dfrac{m}{1.5}\right) = -kt\).

Let \(t\) be the time at which the mass reduces to \(0.5\) gm:
\(\log\left(\dfrac{0.5}{1.5}\right) = -kt \implies \log\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) = -kt \implies -\log 3 = -kt\).

Therefore
\(t = \dfrac{\log 3}{k}\).

Hence the required time during which the mass disintegrates from \(1.5\) gm to \(0.5\) gm is \(\dfrac{1}{k}\log 3\) (in the units of \(t\)), where \(k\) is the decay constant of the element.

Let \(m\) be the amount (in gm) of the substance present at time \(t\) (hours).

The rate of decay is directly proportional to the amount present:
\(\dfrac{dm}{dt} = -k\,m\), where \(k > 0\).

Integrating: \(\log m = -kt + c\), so \(m = m_0\, e^{-kt}\), where \(m_0\) is the initial amount.

Here \(m_0 = 25\) gm, so \(m = 25\, e^{-kt}\).

Two hours later, \(m = 9\) gm (at \(t = 2\)):
\(9 = 25\, e^{-2k} \implies e^{-2k} = \dfrac{9}{25} \implies e^{-k} = \dfrac{3}{5}\).

After one more hour, i.e. at \(t = 3\):
\(m = 25\, e^{-3k} = 25\left(e^{-k}\right)^{3} = 25\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)^{3} = 25 \times \dfrac{27}{125} = \dfrac{27}{5} = 5.4\).

Hence the amount left after one more hour (3 hours in all) is \(5.4\) gm.

Let \(P\) be the population of the city at time \(t\) (years).

The rate of increase is proportional to the population:
\(\dfrac{dP}{dt} = kP\), where \(k > 0\).

Integrating: \(\log P = kt + c\), so \(P = P_0\, e^{kt}\), where \(P_0\) is the initial population.

Take \(t = 0\) at the initial instant, so \(P_0 = 30{,}000\) and
\(P = 30{,}000\, e^{kt}\).

In 40 years the population becomes \(40{,}000\) (at \(t = 40\)):
\(40{,}000 = 30{,}000\, e^{40k} \implies e^{40k} = \dfrac{4}{3} \implies e^{k} = \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)^{1/40}\).

Hence the population at any time \(t\) is
\(P = 30{,}000\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)^{t/40}\).

Equivalently, with \(k = \dfrac{1}{40}\log\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)\), the population is \(P = 30{,}000\, e^{kt}\).

Let \(\theta\) be the temperature of the body (in degrees Celsius) at time \(t\) (minutes). Surrounding temperature \(\theta_0 = 20^\circ\).

By Newton's law of cooling:
\(\dfrac{d\theta}{dt} = -k(\theta - 20)\), where \(k > 0\).

Integrating: \(\log(\theta - 20) = -kt + c\), so \(\theta - 20 = C\, e^{-kt}\).

At \(t = 0\), \(\theta = 100^\circ\): \(100 - 20 = C \implies C = 80\).
So \(\theta - 20 = 80\, e^{-kt}\).

At \(t = 20\) minutes, \(\theta = 60^\circ\):
\(60 - 20 = 80\, e^{-20k} \implies 40 = 80\, e^{-20k} \implies e^{-20k} = \dfrac{1}{2}\).

Let the body cool to \(30^\circ\) after \(t\) minutes:
\(30 - 20 = 80\, e^{-kt} \implies 10 = 80\, e^{-kt} \implies e^{-kt} = \dfrac{1}{8} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{3}\).

Since \(e^{-20k} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), we have \(e^{-kt} = \left(e^{-20k}\right)^{3} = e^{-60k}\), so
\(t = 60\) minutes.

Hence the body takes 60 minutes (1 hour) to cool down to \(30^\circ\) C.

The cone is inverted (apex down) with height 9 cm and base radius 5 cm. Let \(h\) be the depth of water at time \(t\) (seconds) and \(\rho\) the radius of the water surface.

By similar triangles, \(\dfrac{\rho}{h} = \dfrac{5}{9}\), so \(\rho = \dfrac{5h}{9}\).

Area of the water surface:
\(A = \pi \rho^{2} = \pi\left(\dfrac{5h}{9}\right)^{2} = \dfrac{25\pi h^{2}}{81}\).

Given the water level rises at the rate \(\dfrac{dh}{dt} = \dfrac{\pi}{A}\):
\(\dfrac{dh}{dt} = \dfrac{\pi}{\dfrac{25\pi h^{2}}{81}} = \dfrac{81}{25 h^{2}}\).

Separating variables:
\(25 h^{2}\, dh = 81\, dt\).

Integrating from \(h = 0\) to \(h = 9\) (empty to full), and \(t = 0\) to \(t = T\):
\(25 \int_{0}^{9} h^{2}\, dh = 81 \int_{0}^{T} dt\).

\(25 \left[\dfrac{h^{3}}{3}\right]_{0}^{9} = 81\,T\).

\(25 \times \dfrac{9^{3}}{3} = 81\,T \implies 25 \times \dfrac{729}{3} = 81\,T \implies 25 \times 243 = 81\,T\).

\(6075 = 81\,T \implies T = \dfrac{6075}{81} = 75\).

Hence the vessel will be full in 75 seconds.

Let \(A\) be the amount of assets (in rupees) at time \(t\) (years).

The rate of reduction is proportional to the square root of the assets:
\(\dfrac{dA}{dt} = -k\sqrt{A}\), where \(k > 0\) (assets decreasing).

Separating variables:
\(\dfrac{dA}{\sqrt{A}} = -k\,dt \implies A^{-1/2}\,dA = -k\,dt\).

Integrating: \(2\sqrt{A} = -kt + c\), i.e. \(\sqrt{A} = c_1 - \dfrac{k}{2}\,t\).

Initial assets: Rs. 10 lakhs \(= 10{,}00{,}000\), so at \(t = 0\):
\(\sqrt{10{,}00{,}000} = 1000 = c_1\).
Thus \(\sqrt{A} = 1000 - \dfrac{k}{2}\,t\).

After 2 years, assets \(= \) Rs. 10,000, so at \(t = 2\), \(\sqrt{A} = \sqrt{10{,}000} = 100\):
\(100 = 1000 - \dfrac{k}{2}(2) = 1000 - k \implies k = 900\).

So \(\dfrac{k}{2} = 450\) and \(\sqrt{A} = 1000 - 450\,t\).

The person is bankrupt when \(A = 0\), i.e. \(\sqrt{A} = 0\):
\(1000 - 450\,t = 0 \implies t = \dfrac{1000}{450} = \dfrac{20}{9} = 2\dfrac{2}{9}\).

Hence the person will be bankrupt in \(2\dfrac{2}{9}\) years from the start.

Let \((x, y)\) be any point on the curve, and let \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) be the slope of the tangent there.

The slope of the normal at \((x, y)\) is \(-\dfrac{1}{\,dy/dx\,} = -\dfrac{dx}{dy}\).

The normal passes through the point \((2, 0)\), so its slope also equals
\(\dfrac{y - 0}{x - 2} = \dfrac{y}{x - 2}\).

Equating the two expressions for the slope of the normal:
\(-\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{y}{x - 2}\),

which rearranges to
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{x - 2}{y}\).

Separating variables:
\(y\,dy = -(x - 2)\,dx\).

Integrating:
\(\dfrac{y^{2}}{2} = -\dfrac{(x - 2)^{2}}{2} + c_1\),

so \((x - 2)^{2} + y^{2} = C\), where \(C = 2c_1\).

The curve passes through \((2, 3)\):
\((2 - 2)^{2} + 3^{2} = C \implies C = 9\).

Hence the equation of the curve is
\((x - 2)^{2} + y^{2} = 9\),

a circle of radius 3 centred at \((2, 0)\).

Let \(r\) be the radius of the balloon at time \(t\) (seconds), so its volume is
\(V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}\).

The volume changes at a constant rate:
\(\dfrac{dV}{dt} = c\) (constant).

Integrating: \(V = ct + c_1\), i.e.
\(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^{3} = ct + c_1\).

At \(t = 0\), \(r = 3\):
\(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi (3)^{3} = c_1 \implies c_1 = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi (27) = 36\pi\).

At \(t = 3\), \(r = 6\):
\(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi (6)^{3} = c(3) + 36\pi \implies \dfrac{4}{3}\pi (216) = 3c + 36\pi \implies 288\pi = 3c + 36\pi\).

So \(3c = 252\pi \implies c = 84\pi\).

Therefore \(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^{3} = 84\pi\, t + 36\pi\).

Dividing throughout by \(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi\):
\(r^{3} = \dfrac{84\pi\, t + 36\pi}{\tfrac{4}{3}\pi} = 63t + 27\).

Hence the radius after \(t\) seconds is
\(r = (63t + 27)^{1/3}\), equivalently \(r = \sqrt[3]{63t + 27}\).
